If you are pregnant, you should not take ibuprofen unless your doctor tells you to. Taking an NSAID at 20 weeks or later in pregnancy can cause serious heart or kidney problems in the unborn baby and possible complications with your pregnancy. Do not take ibuprofen after 30 weeks of pregnancy.
Ibuprofen may cause a temporary delay in ovulation, which can make it harder to get pregnant. Tell your doctor if you are having trouble getting pregnant.

triples.entity_2: 200 mg to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed
triples.evidence_text: Q: How much ibuprofen can I take and how often? A: Adults can safely take ibuprofen 200 mg to 400 mg (one or two tablets) every 4-6 hours as needed for pain relief. The maximum dose in 24 hours for over-the-counter ibuprofen is 1200 mg (6 tablets of 200 mg each). Ibuprofen is also available on a prescription from a doctor and may be prescribed at a higher strength (600 mg or 800 mg every 6 hours) for severe pain.
